title: The Journal Entries report shows the Close entry on the category account
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to account X at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed today, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports > Journal Entries.
  2. Set the date range to today.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report opens.

Step 2:

  • Work order 1's Close entry shows with account X on the debit side, $80.00, like any entry.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R15: “Reports not named above, checked and unchanged under rule zero: Requested Parts, Payroll Timesheet and the Journal Entries report (which shows the Close and no-charge-line entries with the category account on the debit side like any entry). Customers Spending excludes whole internal and no-charge work orders with the shared predicate of S9-R14; a billable work order with a no-charge line stays in with its invoice total, the line adds $0. Sales Follow Up and Vendors Expenses were removed from ShopView in v26.45.0 (SV-12106); if either returns, it takes the shared predicate then.”
